office_does: The State Senator is the 29th District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.
race_blurb: An open seat after Sen. Steve Conway's retirement, contested by two Democrats: two-term Rep. Sharlett Mena and first-time candidate David Anderson, a Sumner gym owner. They split on the millionaires' tax, spending and data centers.

candidates.summary: Two-term State Representative and chair of the House State Government & Tribal Relations Committee, running on the millionaires' tax, rent stabilization, utility assistance and voting rights.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346 (2026 tax on income over $1 million) and the 2025 capital gains, services and B&O revenue bills [S13][S16][S17][S18]
Voted for EHB 1217 rent limits and campaigns on capping rent increases [S4][S19]
Says she sponsored the Immigrant Workers' Protection Act and the 2026 statewide utility-bill assistance program [S7][S9]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025) and ESSB 5599 (2023), and against Initiative 2113 on police pursuits [S14][S15][S21]
Endorsed by the 29th LD Democrats, Washington State Labor Council, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Fuse Washington [S1][S10][S25]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 and the 2025 capital gains, services and B&O revenue bills, and campaigns on the millionaires' tax and a fairer tax structure.

spending.basis: Backs budgets funding food assistance, K-12, childcare and more resources for high-need school districts; no spending-restraint statements.

housing.basis: Voted for and campaigns on EHB 1217 rent limits; also voted for E2SHB 1110 middle housing, a supply measure.

safety.basis: Voted against Initiative 2113, which loosened limits on police vehicular pursuits; no platform statement on policing.

climate.basis: Leads climate initiatives at Ecology, opposes restarting Centralia coal, and voted for a transmission authority to speed clean-energy build-out.

experience.basis: House member since 2023 and a committee chair, against a first-time candidate; a shorter tenure than a long-serving incumbent.

local-control.basis: Voted for E2SHB 1110, the state mandate requiring cities to allow middle housing in single-family zones.

immigration.basis: Sponsored the Immigrant Workers' Protection Act, lists the National Guard deployment ban, and calls federal enforcement practices unconstitutional.

social.basis: Voted for ESSB 5599, says she opposed restricting LGBTQ+ students including in school athletics, and is a former Planned Parenthood Votes PAC board member.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list and says she advocated for inclusive schools in parental-rights debates.

tech.basis: Says she voted for data-center guardrails (HB 2515) and to end data-center refurbishment tax breaks, and wants data centers to limit ratepayer and water impacts.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and owner of a Sumner ninja-training gym, running on budget restraint, police and mental-health response changes, and blocking new data centers.
highlights: Says Olympia has a spending problem and calls budget management his primary focus [S1][S6]
Says the millionaires' tax violates the state constitution, while proposing higher property tax on homes over $1 million [S3][S5]
Would send social workers rather than police to mental-health calls and wants police focused on theft [S1][S3]
Says no data center will be built in Washington if he is elected [S5]

taxes.basis: Opposes the millionaires' tax as unconstitutional but says he is for taxing the rich and would raise property tax on $1M+ homes while capping it for others.

spending.basis: Repeated statements that the state has a spending problem; pledges to balance the budget and stop 'out-of-control spending.'

safety.basis: Social workers for mental-health calls and treatment over prison, but also fewer legal limits on police for theft and squatting.

experience.basis: No elected experience; says 'I am not a politician' and is running against a sitting legislator.

social.basis: Explicitly backs teaching acceptance of LGBTQ+ youth, more protections for vulnerable communities, and bodily autonomy for women.

tech.basis: Pledges that no data center will be built in Washington if he is elected.
